paper.title: Adaptive Rerank Budgeting for Video-Text Retrieval via Layer-Disagreement Routing
paper.abstract: Two-stage retrieve-then-rerank pipelines are effective for video-text retrieval but face a fundamental efficiency-quality tradeoff: the reranking budget $K$ determines both accuracy and computational cost. We observe that not all queries require the same reranking effort---some are ``easy'' while others benefit from deeper reranking. We propose using \textbf{cross-layer ranking disagreement} as a confidence signal for adaptive budget allocation. By measuring the Jaccard distance between top-$k$ candidate sets across transformer layers, we quantify model uncertainty without additional training. Our 3-tier routing architecture maps disagreement scores to budgets $K \in \{10, 60, 100\}$, allocating more compute to ambiguous queries. On MSR-VTT and DiDeMo benchmarks, our training-free method achieves +0.9 and +1.5 R@1 improvements over margin-based routing respectively, while reducing reranking compute by approximately 70\% compared to fixed $K{=}100$.

content.summary: Noticing the rethink budgeting issue for two-stage retrieve-then-rank video-text retrieval pipelines, the authors propose to adopt cross-layer ranking disagreement to adaptively allocate rethinking budgets. Experiments show that the performance is improved, and the reranking computation is noticeably reduced.
content.strengths: - The idea is easy to understand, and the reported gains are potentially useful.
content.weaknesses:
- The submission appears to be more of a course project instead of a solid publication-level paper. It focused on refining an ad hoc model with minor modifications.

- The method design is ad hoc. For example, selecting the embedding layers as {20, 24, 27} is not shown with solid justifications. The Alt layers setting in Table 2 could also be ad hoc.

- The method design should be better justified. For example, providing an analysis of the correlation between the proposed disagreement indicator and retrieval performance would be helpful.

- The threshold calibration in Sec. 3.4 has not been well clarified. 

- The experiments are not convincing enough. First, given the method's avg-K as 30.9, a baseline with fixed K~31 should also be provided as a reference. Second, the proposed method is only marginally superior on one evaluated dataset and less competitive on the other. Third, the analyses are insufficient. For example, showing the performance curve along with K increasing would be clearer. 

- Visualizations of video-text retrieval samples should be provided.

content.summary: This paper proposes a training-free adaptive reranking strategy for video-text retrieval, tests the hypothesis that cross-layer ranking disagreement reflects model uncertainty, and can guide per-query reranking budget allocation. The method computes Jaccard distance between top-k candidate sets across transformer layers, and uses a 3-tier routing scheme (K ∈ {10, 60, 100}) to allocate compute. Empirical validation on MSR-VTT and DiDeMo shows modest improvements over margin-based routing (+0.9 / +1.5 R@1) while reducing compute by ~70%. The results partially support the hypothesis that cross-layer disagreement is a better confidence signal than embedding margin.
content.strengths:
- Clear motivation/hypothesis
The paper clearly tests cross-layer disagreement is a better uncertainty signal for adaptive reranking than margin.
- Training-free design
No additional training or model modification.
content.weaknesses:
1. Missing comparisons with alternative training-free uncertainty signals such as entropy, score dispersion, and cross-layer score variance.
2. Experiments are conducted on only two datasets and a single backbone (VideoLLaMA3-7B). There is no evidence that the proposed signal generalizes across models.
